synthesis.trait: Directs John with firm, calm command authority -- assigning tasks, denying him entry to the crime scene despite pushback, and enforcing departmental protocol -- while briefly acknowledging John's personal circumstances with some warmth

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Directs John with firm, calm command authority
turning_points.what_changes: In beat6 Sarge's authority is exercised quietly, one-on-one with John (a calm directive plus reassurance). Here he publicly commands and ejects another detective mid-dispute ('McAvoy! Outta here! Now!') and then delivers an explicit, higher-stakes ultimatum to John ('That was the deal... you're door-to-door') -- a more forceful, public exercise of command than the earlier private redirect.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Directs John with firm, calm command authority
turning_points.what_changes: Sarge's 'Got that?' is the unbroken continuation of the ultimatum just delivered in beat12 -- he is pressing for confirmation of the same demand, not introducing a new development.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Directs John with firm, calm command authority
turning_points.what_changes: In beat12 Sarge's composed authority holds against a professional shouting match between officers. Here he stays 'unfazed' and remains entirely focused on securing John's compliance ('Do you understand me, John?') even as a mother collapses in inconsolable grief feet away -- a far more overwhelming disruption than an argument between colleagues, yet his composure and focus on the task hold unchanged.
